newsitem.title: JAPAN: INSTANT VIEW - Japan March merchandise trade data.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Japan March merchandise trade data.

text.p: Below are economists' initial reactions to Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus in March, which fell 26.8 percent from a year earlier to 818.34 billion yen. Japan's surplus with the U.S. rose 11.2 percent
JESPER KOLL, CHIEF ECONOMIST AT JP MORGAN, TOKYO:
"The overall surplus isn't ballooning. Overall import growth into Japan remains very healthy.
"The problem is the bilateral surplus with the U.S. It's America's super-strong economy that is sucking in more imports from Japan -- it's more of a bilateral problem than a global problem."
JASON JAMES, STRATEGIST AT HSBC JAMES CAPEL

"The decline of 27 percent was quite a lot larger than what we had been looking for. There does seems to be a surge of imports coming in to satisfy consumers desire to buy things before the rise in the consumption tax at the beginning in April."
"The underlying trend we've been seeing in recent months is ...for the surplus to start rising and that's just been interrupted by this pre-consumption tax demand."
RICHARD JERRAM, CHIEF ECONOMIST, ING BARINGS JAPAN

"This is just a short-term drop in the surplus and it is likely to start rising again from April, particularly as comparisons are made with, what was in fact, the drop of the trade cycle last April. That was when the seasonally adjusted figures turned around."

"I think that the fact that the overall surplus is down 27 percent but the surplus against the U.S. is up 11 percent is very significant, because that shows that the fears of Robert Rubin and various officials in the U.S. are being confirmed that Japan's trade surplus with the U.S. is going up very sharply." "Even going into the new fiscal year, as the overall trade surplus starts to rise, I think the surplus with the U.S. is going to rise faster than that."
